stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the communities among whom the two tale cycles were first recorded. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Folklorists often trace a tale cycle to the community among whom it was first written down.
• The Salt-Wife tales, in which a fisherman's widow tricks a sea spirit, were first recorded in the 1840s.
• Collectors heard them from herring fishers on the Baltic coast, mostly from women.
• The Lantern Ferryman tales, in which a ferryman tricks a drowned ghost, were first recorded in the 1860s.
• Collectors heard them from barge crews on the Rhine River, mostly from men.
choices: Both the Salt-Wife and the Lantern Ferryman tales center on a protagonist who outwits a supernatural being of the water.
Both the Salt-Wife and the Lantern Ferryman tales were first recorded among fishing communities, one on the Baltic coast.
The Salt-Wife and the Lantern Ferryman tales were each first recorded among people whose daily work kept them on the water.
The Salt-Wife tales were told to collectors mostly by women, whereas the Lantern Ferryman tales were told mostly by men.
explanation: The goal names a specific dimension: the communities where the tales were first recorded. The notes give herring fishers for one cycle and barge crews for the other. These are different jobs, but both groups worked on the water. Choice C names both cycles and states that shared feature with 'each,' so it uses a category that is accurate for both groups. That is the similarity the goal asks you to emphasize.

A.why: You found a real similarity, since both protagonists trick a water spirit, and the word 'both' made it feel right. But it is a similarity in plot. The goal asks about the communities where the tales were recorded. Spotting a similarity is not enough; it has to be the kind of similarity the goal names.

B.why: You picked the right dimension, communities, but you stretched one group's label to cover both. Only the Salt-Wife tales came from fishers. The Lantern Ferryman tales came from Rhine barge crews, who moved cargo rather than fished. A 'both' statement only works if the shared feature is true of both items.

D.why: This is the subtype's main trap. 'Whereas' marks a difference between the storytellers. The goal asks for a similarity, so a choice built on a contrast word fails no matter how accurate it is.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the two studies' results. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Soluble fiber forms a gel in the gut that can trap cholesterol before it is absorbed.
• In 2019, nutrition scientist Priya Raman gave 48 adults a daily oat beta-glucan supplement for 8 weeks.
• Participants' LDL cholesterol fell by an average of 7%; their blood sugar did not change.
• In 2022, nutrition scientist Tomás Ekdahl gave 120 adults a daily psyllium supplement for 12 weeks.
• Participants' LDL cholesterol fell by an average of 7%, and their blood sugar dropped by 4%.
choices: Raman and Ekdahl both gave adults a daily soluble-fiber supplement, oat beta-glucan in one study and psyllium in the other.
Participants in Raman's oat beta-glucan study and Ekdahl's psyllium study saw the same average drop in LDL cholesterol: 7%.
Both Raman's and Ekdahl's studies found that a daily soluble-fiber supplement lowered participants' LDL cholesterol and blood sugar.
Ekdahl's psyllium supplement lowered participants' blood sugar by 4%, whereas Raman's oat beta-glucan left blood sugar unchanged.
explanation: The goal limits you to results, the finding stage of each study. The notes list two results per study, and only one of them is shared: LDL cholesterol fell by an average of 7% in both. Choice B names both studies and joins them under one result ('the same average drop'), so it states that shared outcome directly.

A.why: This is a real similarity, but it is about the studies' methods: what the participants were given. It says nothing about what happened to them. The goal asks about results, so a similarity from the wrong stage of the research does not work.

C.why: You correctly looked at results, then added the second result to both studies. Raman's participants had no change in blood sugar, so this 'both' claim is false for one study. Check that every part of a 'both' statement is true of both items.

D.why: This is the subtype's main trap. It accurately describes a result, but 'whereas' sets up a difference between the studies. The goal asks for a similarity, so any choice built on a contrast word can be eliminated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the nesting behavior of the two populations. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ornithologist Ilse Marrow tracked two songbird populations in southern Portugal for six years.
- The pied flycatchers in the study migrated about 4,000 kilometers to West Africa each winter.
- They nested in tree cavities, and each spring they nested an average of 40 meters from the previous year's nest.
- The Sardinian warblers in the study did not migrate.
- They built open cup nests in shrubs, and their nests in consecutive years were an average of 40 meters apart.
choices: Whereas the flycatchers in the study nested in tree cavities, the warblers built open cup nests in shrubs.
Although only the flycatchers migrated, birds in both populations nested an average of 40 meters from their previous nests.
The flycatchers and the warblers both migrated to the study area each spring to nest close to their earlier sites.
Returning each spring from West Africa, the flycatchers nested an average of 40 meters from their previous nests.
explanation: The goal asks for a similarity in nesting behavior. The notes describe the shared feature in two different ways: the flycatchers nested 40 meters from the previous year's nest, and the warblers' nests in consecutive years were 40 meters apart. Those mean the same thing. B states it for both populations. Its opening clause names a difference, but the main clause carries the similarity, so you shouldn't throw it out just because it starts with 'although.'

A.why: You found a true fact about nesting, but it's a difference between the populations, and 'whereas' marks it as one. The goal asks for a similarity.

C.why: You saw 'both' and stopped checking. The notes say the warblers did not migrate, so they can't have migrated to the study area each spring.

D.why: This gives the shared feature for the flycatchers only. It never says the warblers did the same, so no similarity is stated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the results of the two removal efforts. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2019, ecologists removed invasive reed canary grass from two Minnesota wetlands.
- At Tamarack Marsh, crews cleared 400 square meters by hand.
- By 2022, native sedges had recolonized 120 of those square meters.
- At Heron Fen, crews cleared 150 square meters using controlled burns.
- By 2022, native sedges had recolonized 45 of those square meters.
choices: Native sedges had recolonized 120 square meters at Tamarack Marsh by 2022 but only 45 square meters at Heron Fen.
Both wetlands were cleared of reed canary grass in 2019, though the crews at each site used different methods.
By 2022, native sedges had recolonized 30 percent of the cleared area at both Tamarack Marsh and Heron Fen.
By 2022, native sedges had recolonized most of the area cleared of reed canary grass at both of the wetlands.
explanation: The raw numbers differ (120 and 45), but the proportions match: 120/400 and 45/150 are both 30 percent. C states that shared result for both wetlands. To find the similarity, you have to turn the numbers into the same kind of measure first.

A.why: You compared the raw totals. They do differ, and 'but only' presents them as a contrast, so this choice never shows the similarity in results.

B.why: This is a real similarity, but it's about when the efforts happened, not what they achieved. The goal asks about results. A 'both' sentence on the wrong topic doesn't meet the goal.

D.why: You saw that the outcomes matched but called the shared amount 'most.' Thirty percent is less than a third, so the notes don't support 'most.'

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in how the two planets were discovered. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The transit method detects an exoplanet by measuring the slight dimming of a star as a planet passes in front of it.
- Wenlock-3b, a gas giant, was discovered in 2017 using the transit method.
- It orbits its star every 4 days.
- Arden-7c, a rocky planet, was discovered in 2021.
- Astronomers found it after noticing that its star's light dimmed slightly every 11 days.
choices: Wenlock-3b, a gas giant, was detected by the transit method, whereas Arden-7c is a rocky planet.
Both planets were discovered within the past decade, with only four years between the two discoveries.
Wenlock-3b was discovered by the transit method, and Arden-7c orbits its star once every 11 days.
Like Wenlock-3b, Arden-7c was discovered by the transit method, through the slight dimming of its star.
explanation: The notes never use the words 'transit method' for Arden-7c. They describe it instead: the star's light dimmed slightly at regular intervals, which is exactly what the first note defines as the transit method. Once you see that, the shared feature is the discovery method. D states it for both planets and links them with 'Like.'

A.why: This sets the planets' compositions against each other with 'whereas.' That's a difference, and it gives the discovery method for only one planet.

B.why: This is a real similarity, but it's about when the planets were discovered, not how. The goal names the method.

C.why: This puts two facts side by side without connecting them. It gives Wenlock-3b's method but only Arden-7c's orbit, so it never says the two planets share anything.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the grammar of Tariana and the grammar of Turkish. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tariana is spoken by fewer than 100 people in the Amazon basin of Brazil.
- Tariana verbs carry endings that show whether the speaker saw an event, heard it, or inferred it.
- Turkish is spoken by more than 80 million people.
- Turkish verbs can take the suffix -miş when the speaker learned of an event secondhand rather than witnessing it.
- Tariana and Turkish are not related to each other.
choices: Although the two languages are unrelated, verbs in both Tariana and Turkish can signal how the speaker came to know of an event.
Tariana is spoken by fewer than 100 people in Brazil, whereas Turkish is spoken by more than 80 million people.
Tariana verbs carry endings showing whether the speaker saw an event, heard about it, or inferred that it happened.
Both Tariana and Turkish verbs use endings to distinguish among seeing, hearing, and inferring that an event occurred.
explanation: Both languages mark on the verb how the speaker knows about an event. Tariana separates seeing, hearing, and inferring, and Turkish separates witnessing from secondhand knowledge. A states the shared feature at the level both languages actually have, and the note that the languages are unrelated is subordinate to that point.

B.why: This contrasts how many people speak each language. That's a difference, and it isn't about grammar.

C.why: This describes Tariana's feature well but never mentions Turkish, so no similarity is stated.

D.why: You saw the shared feature and then gave Turkish all of Tariana's detail. The notes show Turkish marking only secondhand versus witnessed, not three separate categories.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the two researchers' methods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2020, paleobotanist Mei Lin studied fossilized seed cones from Patagonia, Argentina.
- She used micro-CT scanning, which builds 3D images from X-rays, to examine the cones without cutting them open.
- She found that the cones belonged to an extinct relative of the monkey puzzle tree.
- In 2023, paleobotanist Daniel Okafor studied fossil fern stems from Antarctica.
- He reconstructed their internal tissues in three dimensions from X-ray images, leaving the specimens intact.
- He concluded that the ferns grew in a warm, wet climate.
choices: Both Lin and Okafor drew conclusions about ancient climates from fossil plants found in the Southern Hemisphere.
Lin and Okafor both used X-ray imaging to study the inside of fossils in three dimensions without damaging them.
Whereas Lin linked her cones to the monkey puzzle tree, Okafor concluded that his ferns grew in a warm, wet climate.
Lin used micro-CT scanning, which builds 3D images from X-rays, to examine fossil seed cones without cutting them.
explanation: The notes call the same technique by different names. Lin's 'micro-CT scanning, which builds 3D images from X-rays' and Okafor's 3D reconstruction 'from X-ray images, leaving the specimens intact' are one method. B states that shared method for both researchers.

A.why: Both fossils do come from the Southern Hemisphere, so the 'both' looks safe. But only Okafor drew a conclusion about climate; Lin's finding was about which plant the cones came from. This choice is also about findings, not methods.

C.why: This contrasts the two findings with 'whereas.' The goal asks for a similarity in methods, and this choice gives a difference in results.

D.why: This describes Lin's method in detail but leaves Okafor out, so it never shows that the methods match.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the fiber the two legumes provide. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- A nutrition study compared two commonly eaten cooked legumes.
- Black beans provided 8 grams of dietary fiber per half-cup serving.
- Dried black beans needed about 90 minutes to cook.
- Split peas provided 16 grams of dietary fiber per one-cup serving.
- Dried split peas needed about 40 minutes to cook.
choices: Black beans provide 8 grams of fiber per half cup, while split peas provide 16 grams of fiber per cup.
Split peas need about 40 minutes to cook, whereas black beans need about 90 minutes to cook.
Black beans and split peas each provide 16 grams of dietary fiber in a single standard serving.
Measured cup for cup, black beans and split peas provide exactly the same amount of dietary fiber.
explanation: The servings are different sizes, so the numbers look different. Eight grams per half cup is 16 grams per cup, the same as split peas. D puts both on the same measure and says outright that the amounts are equal.

A.why: Both facts are here, but 'while' makes 8 versus 16 read as a difference. The sentence leaves the reader to work out the match, so it doesn't emphasize the similarity.

B.why: This compares cooking times with 'whereas.' That's a difference, and it isn't about fiber.

C.why: You spotted that the amounts match but ignored the serving sizes. A black bean serving is a half cup and gives 8 grams, not 16.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in how the two bridges were designed to withstand earthquakes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Corva Viaduct, completed in 1998, is a 1.2-kilometer steel bridge in Chile.
- Its deck rests on rubber-and-lead bearings that absorb ground motion during earthquakes.
- The Nash Strait Bridge, completed in 2016, is a 400-meter concrete bridge in New Zealand.
- It sits on layered rubber pads that soak up seismic shaking before it reaches the deck.
- Its piers are also anchored by deep piles driven into bedrock.
choices: The Corva Viaduct is a 1.2-kilometer steel bridge, whereas the Nash Strait Bridge is a 400-meter concrete bridge.
Both bridges were anchored with deep piles driven into bedrock so that they could resist earthquake shaking.
Both bridges rest on rubber bearings or pads designed to absorb ground shaking during earthquakes.
Completed in 2016, the Nash Strait Bridge sits on layered rubber pads that absorb seismic shaking.
explanation: The notes describe the same protection in different words: 'rubber-and-lead bearings that absorb ground motion' and 'layered rubber pads that soak up seismic shaking.' C names that shared design for both bridges.

A.why: This contrasts length and material with 'whereas.' Those are differences, and neither is about earthquakes.

B.why: This is about earthquake design and uses 'both,' but the bedrock piles belong only to the Nash Strait Bridge. The notes say nothing about piles under the Corva Viaduct.

D.why: This describes only the Nash Strait Bridge's rubber pads. It never says the Corva Viaduct has the same protection, so no similarity is stated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in the source material of the two works. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Hedda Strand's String Quartet No. 2 premiered in Oslo in 1891.
- Its slow movement is built on a cattle call that Strand heard herders sing in Norway's mountains.
- Tomás Ureña's Symphony in A premiered in Madrid in 1903.
- Its finale develops a tune that Ureña transcribed from the singing of shepherds in Andalusia.
- Ureña later published that transcription in a folk-song anthology.
choices: Strand's quartet and Ureña's symphony each build a movement on a melody that the composer heard sung by herders.
Strand's quartet premiered in Oslo in 1891, while Ureña's symphony premiered in Madrid twelve years later.
Both composers later published the herders' melodies they had used in their works in folk-song anthologies.
Ureña's Symphony in A has a finale that develops a tune he transcribed from shepherds singing in Andalusia.
explanation: A cattle call sung by Norwegian herders and a tune transcribed from Andalusian shepherds are the same kind of source: a melody sung by people who tend animals. A states that shared source for both works with 'each.'

B.why: This compares premiere dates and cities. That's a difference, set off by 'while,' and it says nothing about where the music came from.

C.why: You saw the shared herders' melodies and then gave both composers something only Ureña did. The notes don't say Strand published anything.

D.why: This describes Ureña's source accurately but leaves out Strand's quartet, so the two works are never connected.
